diagnoses.preserve: The motivations are missing updates, missing RTSP support, and other firmware not using the latest stock firmware, which includes improvements.
diagnoses.problem: “The answer is simple” adds empty framing, while “new cool stuff” substitutes enthusiasm for a description. The uneven list also leaves readers to infer that RTSP is missing and what is not based on current stock firmware.
diagnoses.quote: The answer is simple: missing updates, RTSP and not based on the latest stock firmware (which features improvements and new cool stuff).

diagnoses.preserve: Credit the other projects and retain the acknowledgment that this version depended on their work.
diagnoses.problem: “Effort and work” duplicates the same idea, and “the making of this new version” adds an indirect construction to an otherwise straightforward acknowledgment.
diagnoses.quote: The effort and work that has been put into the other projects is great and without them the making of this new version wouldn't be possible.

diagnoses.preserve: The reported encoder fixes, retained app functionality, and option to disable that functionality.
diagnoses.problem: “Everything works as it should” is an unbounded assurance. The surrounding text supports particular encoder fixes and tests on named platforms, rather than an unrestricted claim about every function.
diagnoses.quote: Now everything works as it should and the app functionalities are intact (but they can be disabled if you want).

diagnoses.preserve: Gratitude for donations and cameras supplied for testing, and the intention to reward supporters with first access to testing new functionality.
diagnoses.problem: The extended gratitude preamble and “I would like to reward them allowing to be the first ones” bury the concrete early-access benefit in a cumbersome chain of clauses. “Really” adds emphasis without explaining the support.
diagnoses.quote: I'm really thankful to those who supported the project and helped me by donating or sending me new cameras to test on, therefore I would like to reward them allowing to be the first ones to test the new functionalities.

diagnoses.preserve: The distinction between listed firmware features, features in development, and features that might be added.
diagnoses.problem: This introductory sentence repeats the “Features” heading and immediately precedes another “NEW FEATURES” label, creating three layers of framing before any feature appears.
diagnoses.quote: This firmware will add the following features:

diagnoses.preserve: The web server provides statistics and configuration functionality.
diagnoses.problem: “User-friendly” asserts an ease-of-use benefit without identifying any supporting interface behavior. The concrete information here is the availability of statistics and configuration.

diagnoses.preserve: The listed cameras are currently supported; proposed or unsupported models must remain distinguishable.
diagnoses.problem: The sentence repeats the immediately preceding “Supported cameras” heading without adding a support condition or helping readers interpret the list.
diagnoses.quote: Currently this project supports the following cameras:

diagnoses.preserve: Users must verify that their Xiaomi Yi camera is among the supported models in the preceding section.
diagnoses.problem: “A correct Xiaomi Yi camera” leaves the verification criterion vague. The preceding model list supplies the specific criterion: supported-model membership.
diagnoses.quote: Check that you have a correct Xiaomi Yi camera. (see the section above)

diagnoses.preserve: The expected result is a FAT32 partition on the microSD card that enables the camera to load firmware files for the yi-hack-v4 update; retain the protected identifier.
diagnoses.problem: The chain “that will allow … to load … to update to” makes the relationship between the partition and firmware update unnecessarily difficult to follow.
diagnoses.quote: You should now have a FAT32 partition on your microSD card that will allow the camera to load the firmware files to update to

diagnoses.preserve: Every camera-to-filename mapping, both required partition files for each supported model, and the separate “Not yet supported” remark for Yi Home.
diagnoses.problem: This remark repeats the camera name and the requirement already expressed by the row and partition columns. The same boilerplate occupies every supported-camera remark, making the table longer without adding model-specific guidance.
diagnoses.quote: Firmware files required for the Yi Home 17CN / 27US / 47US camera.

diagnoses.preserve: Access the camera's web interface in a browser, retaining the following default hostname and URL instructions.
diagnoses.problem: “Access the web interface … as a website” explains the same action twice, and the following sentence after the hostname repeats the browser-access instruction with the actual address.
diagnoses.quote: Go in the browser and access the web interface of the camera as a website.

diagnoses.preserve: When multiple cameras are present, each needs a unique hostname; otherwise access is only available by IP address.
diagnoses.problem: “It is important to” repeats the immediately preceding “IMPORTANT” label and delays the concrete configuration requirement. The stated consequence already explains why the requirement matters.
diagnoses.quote: It is important to configure each camera with a unique hostname.
